first.rationale: The two live symptoms (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the funnel, and memory_86/memory_31 are the closest matched prior evidence, so simplify_onboarding is my default. But the inherited records are consolidated summaries whose caveats and downstream metrics have been stripped, and the two directions with the largest hidden-cost exposure are exactly the ones in play. I verify memory_86 because 'shorter onboarding lifts completion and time-to-value' is a classic short-horizon win that can mask degraded qualification, weaker week-4+ retention, or completion gains driven by lower-intent accounts — if the original record only measured completion, the memory does not actually support my intended action against a long-term qualified-revenue objective. I verify memory_73 because promotional pricing is the intuitive reflex to a competitor's entry pricing, and discount-led SMB acquisition is the most likely of the five to book revenue that unwinds through churn and margin compression; I want to know whether the original lift was ever measured past the promo window before I let that memory pull the slot. I deliberately do not spend budget on memory_57 (referral) or memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist) since neither addresses the current deficits, and not on memory_91, which I would treat as a fallback if memory_86 fails verification. Scale is a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout: I am acting on unverified-until-checked summaries, the mechanism plausibly trades near-term completion for downstream account quality, and I want retention and qualified-revenue guardrails instrumented alongside completion so the experiment cannot report a win on the same truncated metric that may have produced the original memory. If memory_86's source shows only completion-stage measurement, I will downgrade to activation_messaging or re-scope to test onboarding depth against downstream value directly.
